slides.title: Before you watch
slides.prompt: Imagine the hidden machinery running behind your social media feed.
slides.content:
• The Scale — How many fake accounts do you think exist online right now?
• The Disguise — What might a fake online account look like to fool you?
• Your Feed — Have you ever suspected a comment or account felt strangely inhuman?

questions.question: According to the video, what is a bot?

options.text: A script with a set of instructions
A small automated robot
A program used only for advertising
A fake phone connected to the internet

questions.correctAnswer: A script with a set of instructions

questions.question: Why do bot farms use real phones?

options.text: To make the bots work faster and efficiently
Because platforms trust real devices and block suspicious ones
To give each bot a different script and adapt easier
Because computers cannot run social media in a more realistic way

questions.correctAnswer: Because platforms trust real devices and block suspicious ones

questions.question: What is the main purpose of fake likes, according to the video?

options.text: To make people interact with bots
To increase the number of fake accounts navigating the internet
To make posts look more entertaining
To influence what the algorithm shows people

questions.correctAnswer: To influence what the algorithm shows people

questions.question: Why are bot accounts made to look slightly different from each other?

options.text: To make them harder to be detected
To prevent them from using the same phones
To make their posts more creative and reliable
To reduce the cost of running the bot farm

questions.correctAnswer: To make them harder to be detected

questions.question: What does the speaker mean by “friction”?

options.text: The difficulty of controlling a bot farm
The conflict between real and fake users
The small mistakes and costs involved in real human activity
The time needed to create a social media account

questions.correctAnswer: The small mistakes and costs involved in real human activity

questions.question: Why does the speaker draw the strawberry by hand?

options.text: To make the video more entertaining
To show evidence of human effort and imperfection
To demonstrate how quickly bots can copy images
To explain how artificial intelligence generates pictures

questions.correctAnswer: To show evidence of human effort and imperfection

slides.title: Language focus: Passive voice
slides.content:
Passive voice is the structure that lets you talk about WHAT is done to something without having to name (or care about) who does it — which is exactly how documentaries and explainer clips frame technical processes.
• BE + past participle shifts the focus from the DOER to the thing DONE: "The report was written by the intern".
• Use the passive when the doer is unknown, obvious, or less important than the action.
• The tense of BE tells you WHEN: "is written" (present), "was written" (past), "has been written" (perfect), "will be written" (future).
The lines below are your anchor — every time you drill Passive voice in the next slide, come back to them.

words.translation: Look for BE + past participle in this line from the scene.
Look for BE + past participle in this line from the scene.
words.example: That's why I drew this by hand, not for the style, because a video about fake things had to prove it was made by a real one.

The platform cans push a wave of content to real users.
A bot farm could spreads across a dozen countries.
They cannot to hide behind a fake fingerprint forever.
